title: Travel Protection Plans: Coordination of Benefit Between Certificates
content:
Where a traveller holds more than one Travel Protection Plans policy that answers the same incident, the benefit is coordinated rather than duplicated: the primary policy pays to its own limit and the secondary policy pays only what remains unpaid, up to its own limit.

The primary policy is the one issued first. Where both were issued on the same day, the primary is the one with the larger declared trip cost.

Benefit already consumed on a policy in this term is counted against that policy's limit whatever the claim type, and each claim type is additionally held to its own limit. Benefit consumed in a term is measured over the whole policy term, from the issue date to the expiry or cancellation date, as the total of the amounts paid on that policy together with the amounts recovered against it, taken by benefit claimed.

A deductible is withheld once per claim under the primary policy and is not withheld again under the secondary.

Where the total paid across both policies would exceed the traveller's actual loss, the payment is reduced so that it does not, because protection indemnifies a loss and does not profit from it.

A recovery from a liable third party is applied first to the policy that paid last, restoring its benefit before the primary's.

## Deciding which certificate is primary

| Issue dates | Declared trip costs | Primary certificate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One earlier than the other | Whatever they are | The earlier-issued certificate |
| The same day | One larger than the other | The certificate with the larger declared trip cost |

## Worked coordination on hypothetical figures

Suppose two certificates answer one incident. The primary carries a limit of 1500.00 USD for the benefit claimed and the loss is 2000.00 USD. The primary pays to its own limit, 1500.00 USD, with the deductible its terms call for withheld once. The secondary then answers only what remains unpaid, 500.00 USD, up to its own limit, and no deductible is withheld from it a second time. Had the traveller's actual loss been 1800.00 USD rather than 2000.00 USD, the total paid would be reduced so that it did not exceed 1800.00 USD.

Should a liable third party afterwards pay something back, that recovery is applied to the secondary certificate first, because that is the one that paid last, and only what exceeds its payment reaches the primary's benefit.
